title: Two-sided mind-change register: every strategy entry's adopt test and its abandon test

definitions.adopt: the entry's published 95% interval on (rate - bar) lies entirely above zero
definitions.abandon: that interval lies entirely below zero
definitions.basis: the interval is the one the entry's own table publishes; strategy_results.csv publishes CI_LOW/CI_HIGH on the edge scale, the lab leaderboard publishes hit_rate_ci95 on the rate scale, converted here against the same bar
definitions.bets_to_adopt: n* = ceil((z/|p-p0|)^2 * p(1-p)) at the observed rate - the sample that would clear the bar without the rate moving; a lower bound where the published interval is wider than the normal approximation
definitions.rate_to_adopt: p* = p0 + z*sqrt(p0(1-p0)/n) - the rate that clears the bar at today's n
definitions.no_n: when the observed rate is on the wrong side of the bar, more data cannot promote the entry, and the register says that instead of printing a large n

caveats: This register publishes only the mind-change fields. Promotion still requires the eight validation gates; nothing here moves a strategy's status, and no entry on this board is promoted.

The verdict is read off the interval each table already publishes, so this register can never disagree with the leaderboard page a reader can open. Where the register's own normal-approximation interval would give a different verdict, the row is flagged and no claim is made.
n* is computed under the normal approximation and is a lower bound wherever the published interval is wider; it is the sample needed at the observed rate, not a guarantee of the same rate.
The Week 11 slate had not kicked off when this was registered (2026-11-18), so no row here was written with knowledge of a Week 11 result; the chronology is check F of tools/verify_mind_change.py.
